jobs.title: Why do you want this new job
jobs.description: No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question: âWhy do you want this new job?â In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far: Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years. Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance. Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss. Iâm looking for more challenging work. All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions: I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills. About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer. If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job. About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. Headquartered in San Francisco, our investors include Benchmark , General Catalyst , Peter Thiel , Adam D'Angelo , Larry Summers , and Jack Dorsey . Position: PDF Annotation & Transcription Experts – Korean Type: Contract Compensation: $34/hour Location: Remote Role Responsibilities Source documents by finding publicly accessible Korean PDFs with multimodal elements like images, tables, or diagrams. Record the source of each document. Annotate structure by identifying and bounding every meaningful region of the page. Assign each a component type and a reading-order index. Record relationships by linking each region to its parent component, such as a figure or table. Transcribe faithfully by reproducing all text exactly as it appears in Hangul , including any hanja and handwritten content. Flag any illegible regions. Capture page metadata, including language, document type, source, page dimensions, and flags for tables, formulas, and handwriting. Review a colleague's work. Every task is reviewed end-to-end by a second Korean expert. Qualifications Must-Have Native Korean speaker with full command of Hangul , including hanja . Experience in bilingual transcription, translation, editorial work, or AI training data . Exact character-level accuracy. Systematic application of taxonomy across pages. Comfort with unfamiliar layouts like multi-column newspapers and handwritten forms. Preferred Experience with AI training data : annotation, labeling, grading, or bilingual evaluation. Skills in transcription and localization: MTPE , subtitling, bilingual QA, OCR correction. Document production experience: typesetting, copy-editing, proofreading, or digitization of Korean-language material. Knowledge of script and encoding: Unicode normalization, Korean input methods, Hangul jamo composition, and hanja handling. jobs.title: Competitive Programming Expert - Freelance AI Trainer
jobs.description: Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency. Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment. What this opportunity involves We're building competitive-programming problems and their automatic graders (test cases + checkers) used to train advanced AI coding models. You'll create problems, write both correct and deliberately-wrong solutions, and design the tough test cases that catch subtly-broken code. Your work is what makes the training signal trustworthy. To apply, share: your competitive-programming handle(s) + current/peak rating, any problem-setting experience, and IOI/ICPC/olympiad history. What you'll do Write original algorithmic problems — clear statement, sound constraints, an intended solution; Write correct solutions in C++ and Python; Write realistic wrong solutions (common mistakes) to test against; Build and harden test cases: generators, edge cases, stress and "hacking" tests; Write checkers/interactors (testlib) for problems with more than one valid answer; Confirm the quality bar: correct solutions pass, wrong ones fail, within time limits. What we look for Strong competitive programming background, shown by a public profile — a Codeforces rating (see levels below), OR an IOI / ICPC / national-olympiad record; Fluent contest C++ (STL, complexity); comfortable writing Python; Can explain why a solution is wrong and build an input that breaks it; Strong written English (C1+). Levels (by Codeforces rating, or equivalent olympiad achievement): Associate — 1700–2100 (Expert / Candidate Master): easier problems; Expert — 2200–2600 (Master / Grandmaster): harder problems Senior / Reviewer — 2600+ (Int'l Grandmaster) or IOI/ICPC medalist: hardest problems + quality review. Nice to have IOI / ICPC alumni and top competitive programmers especially encouraged to apply; Experience setting or testing problems for real contests (Codeforces rounds, ICPC, national olympiads, online judges); Testlib experience (checkers, validators, generators); Experience creating data for LLM code benchmarks or similar RL / evaluation datasets. How it works Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid Project time expectations For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10-20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted. Compensation Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $90/hr . Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate. Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Compliance
jobs.description: The short version Every package Portless ships crosses a border, and every one of them carries a set of compliance obligations: how the product is classified, what value is declared, what duties and taxes apply, and what each destination market requires. Today that gets done. It gets done through a mix of partners, internal tooling, and manual work, and it holds together well enough that merchants ship. That's the problem. "Well enough" is not a product, and it isn't a moat. Compliance should be one of the strongest reasons a brand chooses Portless over anyone else. Getting there requires someone who can look at the whole flow end to end, decide what we own versus what we source from the market, and build a coherent system out of what is currently a set of individually reasonable decisions. We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own that. About Portless Portless is changing the face of global e-commerce. By decoupling brands from traditional, expensive domestic warehousing, we let e-commerce companies ship directly from manufacturing hubs to global consumers in as little as three to five days. We move packages to 75+ countries for hundreds of DTC brands, with 2.5 million+ cross-border packages shipped, 99.8% pick-and-pack accuracy, and 98% on-time delivery. We're a small, remote-first team, and the work you do here shows up in a merchant's business within weeks. Why we need this role now Compliance has no clear product direction. We work with multiple compliance partners and we've built real integration infrastructure to support them. What we haven't decided is what Portless itself offers as a compliance product, and that decision is now blocking several others. Build, buy, or partner is an open question with real money behind it. Some of this capability is genuinely commoditized and should be bought. Some of it is close enough to our core that owning it is a differentiator. Nobody has done the work to draw that line and defend it. The data problem is upstream of everything. Compliance decisions depend on product data that originates in merchant catalogs of wildly varying quality, then flows through several systems before it reaches a customs declaration. Every downstream problem traces back to where that data came from and whether anyone validated it. We're operating at a scale where that's now hundreds of thousands of SKUs. The manual work is real and it's growing. Audits, escalations, chasing merchants for missing data, gating SKUs that aren't ready. Our ops and CS teams absorb this today. Product should be removing it, not watching it scale. Merchants can't see any of it. They don't know their compliance exposure, they can't self-serve a fix, and we can't show them the value we're providing. That's a product gap and a commercial one. What you'll own The end-to-end compliance flow. Not one feature area. The whole path from merchant catalog to cleared shipment: where the data originates, how it's validated, where it's enriched, what's stored,

jobs.description: Headquarters: Remote URL: https://www.toptal.com/ About the Role Our client is building an open dataset of real, professional Photoshop work, published on HuggingFace under CC-BY-4.0, to evaluate how well AI systems understand creative editing. Not synthetic tasks. Not staged demos. Actual production work, done the way you already do it. We're looking for working Photoshop artists across six disciplines to complete client-style briefs while a screen recorder captures the session. You work from a brief, you open Photoshop, you do the job. Each task runs roughly 1–3 hours. Your process is the product here. The layer decisions, the masking approach, the moment you undo three steps and take a different route - that's exactly the signal this dataset is built to capture. If you've ever thought AI evaluation of creative work is shallow because the people building it have never actually retouched a beauty shot or built a matte painting, this is your chance to fix that. Rate: $25/hr USD Timeline: This is an extremely urgent role with work starting immediately. If you are interested and apply, please expect to be contacted and requested to complete your account setup on September 9th (Friday), 10th (Saturday), or the 11th (Sunday) to be considered for this role. What You'll Do Complete Photoshop tasks from a client-provided creative brief, working at your normal professional standard Run a client-provided session recorder for the full duration of each task Deliver layered, production-quality PSDs along with final output Work independently, at your own pace, within the scope of each brief Contribute work that will be published openly for research use What You Bring We're recruiting across six specializations and aiming for balanced coverage. Tell us which one is your home turf: Matte painting / digital environments Key visual / campaign compositing Game & UI assets Print & packaging pre-press Portrait / beauty retouching E-commerce / product retouching Hard requirements - please read carefully: Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) with your own licensed copy of Photoshop. Comfortable publishing openly under CC-BY-4.0, meaning the resulting work and session data will be freely available for anyone to use with attribution. Demonstrable professional portfolio in at least one of the six categories above. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/toptal-professional-photoshop-artists
